prompt:
Build a full passenger-vehicle braking model in Simulink or Simscape. The physical plant must include a finite-mass vehicle body with coupled longitudinal, lateral, yaw, roll, pitch and heave motion, four suspension and wheel paths, four distinct tire-road contacts, a powertrain capable of accelerating the vehicle, and four independently actuated wheel brakes.

Accelerate in a straight line toward TargetSpeed_mps and begin the commanded braking maneuver after the vehicle reaches BrakeStartDistance_m. Regulate all four wheel brakes in closed loop using measured vehicle and wheel motion. The anti-lock implementation is unrestricted, but it must modulate the four wheel-brake channels independently when their contact conditions differ. The vehicle trajectory must result from the connected body, suspension, wheel, tire, driveline and brake dynamics; prescribed chassis motion, replayed outputs, duplicated wheel channels and open-loop braking are not valid solutions.

Read TargetSpeed_mps, BrakeStartDistance_m, RequestedDeceleration_g, RoadFrictionScaleHigh, RoadFrictionScaleLow, UseLowFrictionPatch and LowFrictionPatch_m from the MATLAB base workspace. RequestedDeceleration_g is the positive requested longitudinal deceleration expressed as a fraction of standard gravity.

TargetSpeed_mps is a real scalar in [16, 22] m/s; BrakeStartDistance_m is a real scalar in [160, 220] m; RequestedDeceleration_g is a positive real scalar in [0.2, 0.5] g; RoadFrictionScaleHigh and RoadFrictionScaleLow are real scalars in [0.5, 0.8] and [0.2, 0.5], respectively, as dimensionless tire-friction scaling factors; UseLowFrictionPatch is a scalar logical; and LowFrictionPatch_m is a 1-by-4 real vector in m ordered [region start X, region start Y, region length in X, region width in Y]. Use RoadFrictionScaleHigh for the uniform road. When UseLowFrictionPatch is true, apply RoadFrictionScaleLow inside the supplied rectangular spatial region and RoadFrictionScaleHigh outside it, according to each wheel's physical contact location. Support uniform and split-friction braking while limiting wheel lock, yaw and lateral departure.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named VehicleState, WheelState, BrakeState, and TireForceState. VehicleState has 8 channels in this order: longitudinal position X (m), lateral position Y (m), longitudinal and lateral body speed (m/s), longitudinal and lateral body acceleration (m/s^2), yaw angle (rad), and yaw rate (rad/s). WheelState has 12 channels in FL, FR, RL, RR order within each group: four wheel angular speeds (rad/s), four effective rolling radii (m), and four longitudinal slip ratios (1). BrakeState has 12 channels in FL, FR, RL, RR order within each group: four commanded brake pressures, four measured brake pressures, and four ABS-active flags. TireForceState has 8 channels in FL, FR, RL, RR order within each group: four longitudinal and four lateral tire forces (N). Measurements must come from the connected physical and control paths that determine vehicle motion. Save the completed model as cand_XAUTO04.slx in the submission directory.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XAUTO04.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
